subject: Agriculture
title: Rice Paddies of Asia
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Rice Paddies of Asia.

hook.text: Rice paddies look simple—flooded fields with green shoots. Building one is an engineering marvel.

buildup.text: Paddy farming began in China around 7000 BCE. Farmers leveled hillsides into terraces and controlled water flow.

discovery.text: Standing water in paddies suppresses weeds and provides nutrients. Rice yields more calories per acre than wheat.

twist.text: Paddy farming demands intense labor—transplanting seedlings by hand, one by one, into flooded mud.

climax.text: This labor-intensive system fed billions. Asia's population density traces directly to rice cultivation.

punchline.text: One grain, one technique—it fed half the world.

quiz.question: Why does rice yield more calories per acre than wheat?
options: Flooded paddies suppress weeds and concentrate nutrients
